added_lines: sacristan: ciarán ryan 30th sunday in ordinary time - 23rd / 24th october 2026 we remember in our prayer at mass this weekend the following whose anniversaries and month’s mind occur at this time: jimmy slevin michael king chris hehir michael hehir joe kelly kitty mcevoy henry leonard (month’s mind) josephine smith fidelma & jerry neville from the deacon’s desk this sunday’s readings exodus 22:20-26 & matthew 22:34-40. living the commandment of love this sunday's readings bring us to the very heart of god's law. in the first reading from exodus, god reminds his people that genuine faith is expressed not only in prayer and worship but also in the way we treat others, especially those who are vulnerable. the israelites are instructed not to oppress the stranger, exploit the poor, or neglect those in need. having experienced hardship themselves, they are called to show compassion, justice and mercy to others. in the gospel, jesus is asked which commandment is the greatest. his answer unites the whole of god's law into two inseparable commands: to love god with all our heart, soul and mind, and to love our neighbour as ourselves. love of god and love of neighbour are not separate duties but two dimensions of the one christian calling. these readings challenge us to examine how our faith is lived in everyday life. it is easy to profess belief in god; it is often more demanding to show patience, kindness and understanding to those around us. jesus reminds us that the measure of our love for god is reflected in the care, respect and compassion we show to others. in loving our neighbour, we reveal the presence of god's love in our world. deacon eric thank you to fr kevin with fr kevin’s recent departure to his new appointment in wicklow, we would like to offer parishioners an opportunity to express their gratitude for his seven and a half years of faithful service to our parish. anyone wishing to contribute to a presentation for fr kevin can do so using the envelopes available at the back of the church. these may be placed in the collection boxes or returned to the parish office. rev eric cooney coordinator of parish administration mobile:
